items.stem: Under the 1987 Constitution, what does the Philippines renounce as an instrument of national policy?

reveal.why_correct: Art. II, Sec. 2 says: "The Philippines renounces war as an instrument of national policy."

why_wrong.o3: Diplomacy is a peaceful tool the State keeps using.
why_wrong.o2: Trade is not renounced anywhere in Art. II.
why_wrong.o4: The State still enters treaties; Art. VII, Sec. 21 sets how.

items.stem: How many persons compose the Commission on Human Rights under the 1987 Constitution?

reveal.terms: The CHR is an independent office created by Art. XIII, Sec. 17.
reveal.shortcut: CHR: 1 Chairman + 4 Members.
reveal.why_correct: Art. XIII, Sec. 17(2): "The Commission shall be composed of a Chairman and four Members who must be natural-born citizens of the Philippines and a majority of whom shall be members of the Bar."

why_wrong.o3: Chairman plus two is the make-up of the CSC and COA (Art. IX-B, IX-D), not the CHR.
why_wrong.o2: Chairman plus six is the COMELEC (Art. IX-C).

items.stem: A CHR team arrives unannounced at a municipal jail to inspect how detainees are treated. Which constitutional power of the Commission is it using?

options.text: Power to amend the Rules of Court
Visitorial powers over jails, prisons, or detention facilities
Power to prosecute and convict offenders

reveal.terms: Art. XIII, Sec. 18 lists the CHR's powers and functions.
reveal.shortcut: Jail inspection = visitorial powers, Sec. 18(4).
reveal.why_correct: Art. XIII, Sec. 18(4): the CHR shall "Exercise visitorial powers over jails, prisons, or detention facilities."

why_wrong.o4: Pardons belong to the President (Art. VII, Sec. 19).
why_wrong.o3: The CHR investigates; it does not prosecute or convict.
why_wrong.o1: The Supreme Court promulgates the Rules of Court (Art. VIII, Sec. 5(5)); the CHR only adopts its own rules.

items.stem: A suspect is being questioned by police about a theft and cannot afford a lawyer. What does the Bill of Rights require?

options.text: A barangay official may serve as counsel
Counsel must be provided to the suspect
The suspect must first post bail
Questioning may continue without counsel if the suspect is cooperative

reveal.terms: Art. III, Sec. 12(1) covers rights of a person under investigation.
reveal.shortcut: Can't afford counsel? One must be provided.
reveal.why_correct: Art. III, Sec. 12(1): the person "shall have the right ... to have competent and independent counsel preferably of his own choice. If the person cannot afford the services of counsel, he must be provided with one."

why_wrong.o4: The right to counsel does not depend on cooperation; it can be waived only in writing and in the presence of counsel.
why_wrong.o3: Bail is a separate right (Sec. 13) and is not a condition for counsel.
why_wrong.o1: Counsel must be competent and independent; the text does not allow a substitute official.

items.stem:
Passage: The municipal treasurer's office moved its payment counter to the ground floor in June. Before the move, senior citizens had to climb two flights of stairs, and many asked relatives to pay for them. In July, the office recorded 40% more payments made in person by senior citizens than in May. The treasurer said the office will also add a second counter if the line stays long in August.

What is the main point of the passage?

options.text: Stairs are dangerous in all public buildings
Relatives should stop paying for senior citizens
The treasurer's office will close in August
Moving the counter made in-person payment easier for senior citizens

reveal.terms: Answer only from what the passage states or clearly implies.
reveal.shortcut: Find the sentence that answers the question.
reveal.why_correct: The passage is about the counter move and its effect on senior citizens.

why_wrong.o3: Nothing says the office will close.
why_wrong.o2: The passage reports a fact; it gives no such advice.
why_wrong.o1: Too broad: the passage is about one office.

items.stem:
Arrange the sentences into a logical paragraph.
S. Next, the clerk checks that every required field is filled in.
P. First, the applicant gets the form from the front desk.
Q. Finally, the applicant receives a claim stub with a release date.
R. The applicant then submits the completed form to the records clerk.

reveal.terms: Look for the opener and the transition words (first, then, however, as a result).
reveal.shortcut: Find the sentence that needs nothing before it.
reveal.why_correct: First (P) → then submits (R) → next, clerk checks (S) → finally, claim stub (Q).

why_wrong.o2: The clerk can't check the form before it is submitted.
why_wrong.o1: R says "then", so it cannot open the paragraph.

Arrange the sentences into a logical paragraph.
P. As a result, the office now prints only the pages it needs.
Q. The supply officer noticed that paper costs doubled in one quarter.
R. She traced the rise to full reports being printed for every meeting.
S. She proposed sending reports by email and printing only summaries.

reveal.terms: Look for the opener and the transition words (first, then, however, as a result).
reveal.shortcut: Find the sentence that needs nothing before it.
reveal.why_correct: Problem noticed (Q) → cause traced (R) → proposal (S) → result (P).

why_wrong.o2: "She" in R needs Q first to say who she is.
why_wrong.o1: The proposal (S) depends on the cause found in R.
why_wrong.o3: Reversed: "As a result" closes the paragraph.

items.stem:
Using standard alphabetic filing, which name is filed FIRST?
Atty. Carlos Dizon | Ma. Lourdes de la Cruz | Benito Delgado | Ramon Dizon Jr.

reveal.terms: Index each name into units, then compare unit by unit, letter by letter.
reveal.shortcut: Apply ARMA Rule 6 first.
reveal.why_correct: Index units: DelaCruz, Delgado, Dizon Carlos (Atty. last), Dizon Ramon (Jr. last). "Dela" < "Delg", so De la Cruz is first. This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 6), not a rule published by the CSC.

why_wrong.o3: Atty. is the last unit, so this files as Dizon Carlos, after the D-e names.
why_wrong.o4: Delgado comes after DelaCruz (a < g at the 4th letter).
why_wrong.o1: Jr. is a last unit; Dizon still files after Del- names.

items.source: Civio Filing Rules v2 / ARMA Rule 6

items.stem:
Using standard alphabetic filing, which business name is filed FIRST?
Ace Printing | 3 Sisters Bakery | Bright Star Hardware | Alpha Office Supply

reveal.terms: Index each name into units, then compare unit by unit, letter by letter.
reveal.shortcut: Apply ARMA Rule 7 first.
reveal.why_correct: Under ARMA Rule 7, names that begin with digits file before names that begin with letters. This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 7), not a rule published by the CSC.

why_wrong.o4: Letters file after digits, and B comes after A.
why_wrong.o2: Ac comes before Al, and in any case letter names file after the digit name.

items.stem:
Using standard alphabetic filing, which name is filed LAST?
Dr. Elena Santos | Elena Santos-Reyes | San Jose Pharmacy | Engr. Elmer Santos

reveal.terms: Index each name into units, then compare unit by unit, letter by letter.
reveal.shortcut: Apply ARMA Rule 3 first.
reveal.why_correct: Units: SanJose Pharmacy (Rule 6), Santos Elena Dr, Santos Elmer Engr, SantosReyes Elena (Rule 3: hyphenated is one unit). SantosReyes is longest after Santos, so it is last. This follows the standard office filing rule (ARMA International Simplified Filing Standard Rules, Rule 3), not a rule published by the CSC.

why_wrong.o1: Dr. is the last unit; this files as Santos Elena, before SantosReyes.
why_wrong.o3: San Jose is one unit, SanJose, which files before Santos.
why_wrong.o2: Engr. is the last unit; Santos Elmer still precedes SantosReyes.

items.source: Civio Filing Rules v2 / ARMA Rule 3
